messages:
ajay (infra): Heads-up — had a call with AWS earlier. They're open to a custom GPU EDP but want clearer demand profiles and a proposal for recovery SLAs.

kevin (aws-sales): thanks Ajay. we can do a dedicated commitment with a regional floor + burst pool. need to confirm which regions and the minimum monthly spend. also need a 99.9% GPU host availability SLA for reserved pools.

maria (eng-infra): quick note — our current steady-state is ~320 A100-equivalent hours/day across us-west-2 + eu-west-1, with 40% weekly variance due to training bursts. can provide per-week timeseries.

sophie (finops): can you convert that to committed $ amount? use current list price discount tiers so we have a baseline to compare. i'd ballpark $120k/mo at on-demand but we expect EDP to be significantly lower.

kevin (aws-sales): that helps. if you commit 12 months, we can look at a 28-34% list discount and a 10% buffer credit for burst usage above the committed floor, subject to region caps. the SLA reclamation procedure requires a 4-hr notice and 3rd-party capacity relocation if local pool is impacted.

jordan (cloud-ops): 4-hour reclamation is too long for production-facing inference traffic. any chance for faster fallback or automatic routing to a fallback model pool?

kevin (aws-sales): we can add an automatic fallback clause to route to compatible VM families in another AZ within 30-60 minutes, but cross-region fallback increases egress/cost complexity.

rita (aws-accounts): on credits — we can offer a one-time credit equal to 5% of committed spend if we miss the availability SLA more than twice in a quarter.

sophie (finops): credits are fine but we prefer service credits tied to measured customer impact (tokens served / latency). a pure dollar credit doesn't incentivize low-latency fallbacks.

ajay (infra): proposal from our side: 12mo commitment, floor sized to cover 70% of steady-state (0.7 * 320 hours/day) across the two regions, with a 20% burst buffer pool funded by AWS credits. SLA: 99.95% reserved host availability; recovery path <60 minutes to fallback-compatible pool; penalty = 5% monthly invoice per missed SLA event, escalates after 2 repeated misses.

kevin (aws-sales): i'll need to loop in legal, but high level that sounds workable. 99.95% is above our standard for reserved GPU pools; they typically sit at 99.9% — raising to 99.95% will require a pricing delta. can you share the weekly timeseries and a list of peak windows?

maria (eng-infra): attaching a quick summary (pasted):
```
week_start,avg_hours_per_day,95pct_hours_per_day,peak_hour_window
2026-01-05,310,420,Mon 02:00-06:00 UTC
2026-01-12,340,490,Thu 18:00-22:00 UTC
2026-01-19,300,380,Wed 01:00-04:00 UTC
2026-01-26,360,540,Tue 20:00-23:00 UTC
```

jordan (cloud-ops): note: those peaks are mostly model fine-tune jobs that tolerate preemption if we have a warm cache for checkpoints. inference latency-critical routes cannot preempt. must ensure reserved pool capacity maps to inference fleets, not purely training.

kevin (aws-sales): good distinction. we can carve separate SKU buckets: reserved-rt (inference) and reserved-batch (training). reserved-rt will have better availability and a higher price.

sophie (finops): give me two numbers: 12mo committed spend for a 70% floor with reserved-rt weighting (x% of the floor), and the delta to lift SLA from 99.9% -> 99.95%. i'll model TCO vs our current Dedicated cluster costs.

rita (aws-accounts): also consider metering nuance: sustained vs bursting. our metering system timestamps usage at allocation start, not token-emit. we can include a clause to reconcile overage bursts monthly with a TTL-based aggregation to avoid spiky charge multipliers.

amajay (typo?) —

ajay (infra): (typo) — rita, that TTL reconciliation sounds useful. we want burst smoothing so we don't get billed per-second noise from autoscale. can you outline the reconciliation window you'd propose?

rita (aws-accounts): propose 1-hour rolling aggregation for metering during bursts, plus a monthly reconciliation that looks at 95th percentile of hourly usage and applies committed floor credits accordingly.

kevin (aws-sales): i'll draft a term sheet with: commitment numbers, regional floor split, reserved-rt carve-out, SLA targets and credit formulas, burst buffer credit description, and metering reconciliation. expect it tomorrow EOD.

maria (eng-infra): reminder — confirm also whether GPUs are dedicated hosts or shared instances. dedicated hosts are preferred for security/compliance and stable perf.

kevin (aws-sales): noted. dedicated host support will be an add-on; pricing in term sheet.

sophie (finops): please include early-termination terms and migration support. we need 90-day notice windows and pro-rated refunds for unused commitment if infra changes force a migration.

ajay (infra): thanks everyone. action items: kevin to send term sheet; rita to detail metering TTL; maria to send final 12-week timeseries; sophie will run TCO model once term sheet arrives. pinging @kevin (aws-sales) :thumbsup:

billing-bot: invoice-forecasting: upcoming: your projected monthly utilization vs commit shows a 15% upside to committed floor in next quarter based on queued jobs. consider increasing floor or negotiating larger burst pool.

kevin (aws-sales): saw billing-bot note — we can include a one-time growth window at month 3 to re-evaluate floor sizing without penalty.

jordan (cloud-ops): perfect. that flexibility makes us comfortable to close faster.

sophie (finops): ok — i'll prioritize the TCO run once term sheet lands. thanks all. :rocket:
